mappings.note: Which statement about Grandpa's cover story is correct (he said Ravi disappeared). Plot recall; this chapter has no LO for plot, since LO-15 to LO-17 are poem outcomes, LO-18 is a character sketch and LO-19 is grammar.
What Grandpa brought out (a gift-wrapped parcel) -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
Why the mother was impatient about the gift (Ravi's birthday was three months earlier) -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
What occasion was actually being celebrated (Grandpa's own birthday) -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency. The interpretive version of this, the irony it produces, is mapped separately to LO-17.

What the tradition of giving gifts on his OWN birthday REVEALS ABOUT HIS CHARACTER -- generosity, against distractors of forgetfulness and selfishness. C-2.2-LO-18, character inferred from an action the text only shows.
What was inside the parcel (a detective storybook) -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
Grandpa's facial expression (a mischievous wink) -- recall of a stated detail, C-2.2 competency. Not LO-18: the item asks what the expression was, not what it shows.
The advice to read up on how to 'trail a suspect' -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.

What 'Vitamin-M' stands for (Memory vitamin) -- recognition of the term. C-2.2 competency; LO-17 is reserved here for the two items that ask what the term MEANS in the story rather than what it expands to.
Which option states the main irony -- recognition among four candidate ironies, C-2.2 competency. The item that asks the student to EXPLAIN the irony is mapped to LO-17.
Why Grandpa had to move to the city -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
What he missed most about his hometown (the brick house, the mango tree) -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.

Which incidents prompted the mother's worry (the double dose, the forgotten route) -- plot recall. Not C-2.1-LO-8, which requires the treatment of memory here to be set beside other writing about growing old.
How the mother TREATED Grandpa and HOW IT AFFECTED HIM -- her manner read as character, and its effect on him. C-2.2-LO-18. Not C-3.2: no judgement on whether she was right is asked here.
Why Ravi felt guilt -- his empathy inferred from what he observes, never stated outright. C-2.2-LO-18.
What the secret mission was and why it was given -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
How Grandpa spent his time at the park -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
Which 'banned' foods he treated himself to -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.

Describe Ravi's physical efforts to stay hidden -- crouching, crawling, ducking. C-2.2-LO-15 would fit the action verbs as sensory imagery, but it is written as 'imagery in the POEM' and this is the prose story, so C-2.2 competency.
The embarrassing situations Ravi faced -- angry vendors, eviction from the salon. Plot recall, C-2.2 competency. DEFECT: the stem ends with page furniture, 'NODIA PAGE 384 CBSE CLASS 9 ENGLISH R1'.
How Grandpa outsmarted Ravi at the bus stop (the swapped yellow cap) -- the event itself, C-2.2 competency. The item asking what the event does to the pair's relationship is mapped separately.

How Ravi felt on realising he was tracking a stranger -- the text states the horror, so this is recall rather than inference, C-2.2 competency. Not LO-18, which I reserve for what the text shows without stating.
What Ravi found on rushing home (Grandpa asleep and snoring) -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
How Ravi reacted on seeing Grandpa safe (a warm hug) -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
The cover story Grandpa told his daughter -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
What the gift was and why the mother objected -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.
What occasion was actually being celebrated -- plot detail, C-2.2 competency.

Why a detective storybook was a HUMOROUS gift -- the joke depends on reading the wink and the failed surveillance together. Interpreting meaning, C-2.2 competency; CG-2 names humour as a genre but neither C-2.1 LO here covers it (LO-7 is poem form, LO-8 is writing about ageing). Reported as a frame gap.

What 'Vitamin-M' REFERS TO IN THE CONTEXT OF THE STORY -- the title term read as the story's central figure, supported from the mother's behaviour. C-2.2-LO-17, whose wording says 'of the poem' although the text is prose; cited on substance and flagged.

EXPLAIN the situational irony about memory -- the mother who polices Grandpa's memory forgets her own father's birthday. The central conceit interpreted and supported from the text, C-2.2-LO-17. Distinguished from the MCQ that only asks which option names the irony.
A detailed character sketch of Grandpa balancing vulnerability against sharp wit -- C-2.2-LO-18 in its fullest form, and the concept tag 'Character Analysis' agrees.

Two halves: analyse the mother's character (C-2.2-LO-18) and judge whether her INTENTIONS JUSTIFY her treatment of Grandpa (C-3.2, weighing premises to reach a defended verdict). Both cited because the second half is an argument, not a sketch.

How the theme of elderly independence against overprotective caregiving is DEVELOPED THROUGH THE NARRATIVE -- thematic close reading across the whole story. No LO covers theme here (LO-17 is the central symbol, LO-18 a character), so C-2.2 competency.

Write a diary entry AS RAVI about his guilt and his failure as a detective -- first person, the day's events plus his response to them, which is C-1.3-LO-4 exactly. Not C-1.2: the LO names this form, so competency level would lose precision.
Describe the bus-stop climax and say how it shifts the POWER DYNAMIC between Grandpa and Ravi. Structural and relational reading rather than a character sketch, so C-2.2 competency rather than LO-18.
